description: Oregon Women's Land Trust has bought 145 acres in southern Oregon, as part of an effort to give women control over their own destinies through land trusts, available to all women and children whether to live there or just stop, camp out, and relax.
raw_text: LAND TRUSTS FOR WOMEN is an effort to give women control over their own destinies. Two groups of women have researched the concept of land trusts, and formed groups to acquire land for all women and children at all times. This would promote the spiritual, emotional, physical, cultural, and economic well-being of women, and preserve the land. Many of us love nature deeply, and need to live with green all around us and be self-sufficient. We feel caged in polluted, violent cities where we survive day to day by doing meaningless work or by standing in welfare lines. Financially poor women are unable to buy rural property. Private ownership creates hassles anyway. Putting land in a land trust removes it from the speculative market. It would be available to all women and children, whether they want to live there or just stop for a short time, camp out, and relax. We can help women set up local land trusts, or they can join us. Oregon Women's Land Trust has bought 145 acres in southern Oregon. Write OWLT, Box 1713, Eugene, OR, 97401, or California Women's Land Trust, c/o Carole & Yolanda, 1538 N. St. Andrews, Hollywood, CA, 90028.

description: Has "secured" 80 acres in northwest Arkansas as the beginning of a women's land trust; still researching how to form the trust. Will live only with dykes and relate to female children only. No buildings yet; plans to stress farming to feed women on the land and in the cities; needs money to pay off the land. Emphasizes the need to work. No dogs.
raw_text: WOMEN ON LAND has "secured" 80 acres of land in northwest Arkansas as a beginning for a women's land trust. We are investigating and researching the details of how to form a land trust. We believe a land trust is a way each woman involved with this land can have equal access and responsibility to the land to the feminist community. The concept of a land trust can take care of legal trips and power trips. The land can be legally "owned" by the land trust and each woman could have lease for lifetime use of the land. There is much to be worked out, but we want you to know that no woman woman will get ripped off after putting in her time, energy, work, or money. It is difficult to review all the research and energy into laws, qualifying to fit their rules, and at the same time, trying to build a new culture, but we have to use their laws for some measure of protection against them. We will live only with dykes. We wish to relate to female children only - male children would be too sexist an influence on a developing women's environment. We want to stress farming on this land to raise food to feed the women on the land and support sisters in the cities. There are no buildings on the land, just 80 acres of beautiful trees, a waterfall, a creek, and lots of painful bugs. We need to share the responsibility for getting money to pay off the land, for gathering tools, building materials, seed, horse, windmill. We are open to any woman who wants to relate to this land whether she wants to stay full-time, work for the summer, camp and work, spend the weekend, or stay here on the way cross country. We do want to emphasize the need to work. When you write, describe yourself, your politics, what you can offer and why you want to come. (No dogs please.) Send a stamped, self-addressed envelope to Women on Land, PO Box 521, Fayetteville, Arkansas, 72701.
notes: Typed as Intentional Community/Cooperative: the group appears to be living on the land already ("We will live only with dykes"). The land is "secured" (the listing's quotation marks) but not yet paid off; an unpaid mortgage alone does not make it a land fund. Accepted groups from "We will live only with dykes" and "female children only"; the listing also says it is open to "any woman who wants to relate to this land," which is in tension with this. description: A small lesbian farm in the eastern foothills of the Cascades. Two women and one child, with many visitors, began rebuilding an old farm valley as a place for all women to work, live, or visit: a cabin to become a community center, a well, a chicken coop, a sauna. Planned a children's space, a playground, an herb garden, a June festival, and health workshops.
raw_text: SAPPHA SURVIVAL SCHOOL is a small lesbian farm in the eastern foothills of the Cascade mountains in Washington. One woman who stayed there for a week last summer wrote the following about SSS. "Two women and one child, with many visitors, started this spring to rebuild an old farm valley into a place for all women to work and live, or visit. I helped rebuild the old cabin, later to be the community center, helped dig a well, and build a chicken coop. Freedom and Dykepride run strong - the valley is isolated enough to remove society's inhibitions and its censure of lesbians. Olivia Newton Outhouse is presently open to the sky and a valley view, stream water is pumped to flow between pine branches for the shower and half naked Amazons are everywhere! Evening relaxation is often a sauna, fueled by hot rocks and followed by a dip in the stream." This summer they planned on more structures including a children's space scaled to their size, and an outrageous playground scaled to everybody's size. They also planned an herb garden, a festival in June, and workshops on health. To find out more, write: SSS, Box 4D, Aeneaes Valley Road, Tonasket, WA, 98855.

raw_text: ANOTHER DEMENTION is opening soon to accomodate women who are seeking a space on the land working together with other women in areas of recreation, farming, and general growing. 70 acres will be available for camping and/or year-round living in beautiful wilderness area of Oklahoma near Tishomingo, capitol of the chicasaw nation. A variety of flora and fauna abound in the area of the wildlife refuge 3 miles away and can be enjoyed while canoeing down the blue river or pennington creek. Wild mustangs adopted through the government will be among the horses in residence eager to offer alternative means of transportation around the area for exploration and enjoyment. Womancraft can be sold in distribution outlet store on roadfront or consigned to be distributed by the MAGIC FERRY to the FERRY DYKINGS and other contact points across the country. Women in residence will maintain their own shelter and be responsible for their own life-support needs. A community garden will be the major food source operating on cooperative energy. Monthly rate for any number of days spent on the land is $5.00, payable on or before each new moon. This money will be used for payment of the land. Financial priorities are pressing now - money is being raised to expedite the negotiations and be on the land within 30 days. We are a non-profit association and any donation is tax-exempt. Send any contributions to: Sisters of Diana, Inc., RR1, Box 42A, Tishomingo, OK, 73460. Loan contracts also honored.

raw_text: WOMANSHARE is a feminist country retreat. It is run by a collective of five women who open their house for workshops to women seeking more about themselves and their lives. They say, "we feel that living with each other in the country has helped us to become stronger, healthier, more centered, and more creative. Some of the things we have been dealing with are our feminist politics, our sexuality and our own creativity. We know that we need contact with other women and we also need to find a way to survive economically in the country. Womanshare is our way of doing this." Fees are on a sliding scale from $10 to $15 per day. Scholarships are available and child care is negotiable. Include partial payment $10) when you register. The Womanshare Collective says, "we would like you to come and relax, join in discussion groups and workshops, enjoy good home-cooked food, and get to know us. We feel that being in the country, having a good time with other women can be a very high experience." For more information, write Womanshare, 1531 Gray's Creek Road, Grants Pass, OR, 97526. Thanks to RUNES for this info.

It is a special place where women may come together away from the daily hassles of the patriarchal society and experience the strength of a woman's culture. It is not a resort. Each woman who comes to the land makes a commitment to herself and other women thereby accepting responsibility for herself, as well as by respecting and supporting other sisters who are there. Womens Ways is located in the rolling Berkshire mountains in Craryville, New York. There is a large A-frame house built solely by women. Camping is available for $2.50 a night or $40.00 a month and access to the house and utilities is available. Work exchanges are also available, as there is never a lack of projects around. Anyway you could add that we'd like to hear from any of your readers who are seriously interested in biodynamic agriculture or conservation/ecology action. Furthermore, I'd like to point out again that we don't own Feathers Farm, at least not yet, and that even groups with more people and a deed are usually burdened, as we are, with immense ongoing financial pressures. I mention this because I have noticed recurring and unrealistic attitudes toward "wimmin on land" which range from idealizing our self-sufficiency to guilt-baiting out non-urban "privileges." Our desire to share the experience of the land is large and sincere (hospitality is central in our value system), but we are also thus more vulnerable to getting ripped off or imposed upon by bad attitudes. I applaud the Land Directory and your generous efforts in making it happen, hoping it is a big step toward valuable networking among the land groups themselves, as well as a way for us to reach out to travelling and urban lesbians. But it is important, in my opinion, for the "sisterhood" and the very survival of land groups to discuss and understand what can and often does go wrong, why groups don't make it, how to build a political analysis beyond our interactions with each other, the land and sexual identities. Let us not get too smug about "3000 acres of women-owned land" - we could fr'instance do another questionnaire to find out just what are all these wimmin doing on land, how many of us are actually secure in a modest financial sense? How might urban wimmin find appropriate ways to fit into our constant reality and vice versa? --Thanks, Peggy Gallagher, Feathers Farm, Box 19, Bryantville, MA 02327 (617)585-8826
